questions.q: Which of these is a positive statement?
options: The UK should cut income tax
Inflation is the most serious problem the UK faces
An increase in the price of bus fares will reduce the number of bus journeys
It is unfair that some people earn so much more than others
questions.why: It makes a claim about cause and effect that could be checked against data. The others contain value judgements (should, most serious, unfair).

questions.q: Which of these is a normative statement?
options: The Bank of England ought to lower interest rates
A tax on cigarettes raises their price
Wages in London are higher than in Wales
questions.why: "Ought to" shows a value judgement about what should happen. The others could be tested against evidence.

questions.q: "A rise in the minimum wage will put 5 million people out of work" is a normative statement, because it is almost certainly untrue.
questions.why: It is a positive statement. Positive means testable, not true: this claim could be checked against evidence, and would probably be shown to be wrong.

questions.q: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: All other things stay the same
A simplified picture of how the economy works
questions.why: Positive statements are testable; normative ones rest on values. Ceteris paribus holds other factors fixed so a model can focus on one change.

questions.q: Why is economics called a social science rather than a natural science like chemistry?
options: It studies human behaviour and usually cannot run controlled experiments
questions.why: Economists use the scientific method, but they study people, who react and change, and they cannot hold a whole economy still to experiment on it.

questions.q: An economist predicts that a rise in the price of coffee will reduce the amount bought, ceteris paribus. What does "ceteris paribus" add to the prediction?
options: It means the prediction is certain
It assumes other things, such as incomes and tastes, do not change at the same time
It means the prediction is normative
It means the price rise is caused by the government
questions.why: Ceteris paribus holds everything else constant, so the model can isolate the effect of the price change. In the real world other things often do change.

questions.q: Two economists agree on what a sugar tax would do to sugar consumption and tax revenue, but one supports it and one opposes it. Explain how this can happen.

ideas.label: Policy choices involve value judgements (opinions), not just evidence
They weigh the outcomes differently, e.g. health against freedom or fairness to poorer households

questions.model: The evidence (the positive part) only shows what is likely to happen. Deciding whether that is worth it needs value judgements: one economist may put more weight on better health, the other on personal freedom or on the tax hitting poorer households hardest.
questions.why: Agreeing on the positive economics still leaves the normative choice: how much each outcome matters is a value judgement.

tests.answer: Because whether to have the tax is a value judgement. One cares more about health, the other thinks it is unfair on poor households.
They have different opinions about it.
One of them has worked out the numbers wrong.
